generated-coordinate-no-leading-lf-wrong.title: Assertion checks the wrong generated Kotlin line
generated-coordinate-no-leading-lf-wrong.description: The supplied Kotlin string begins with `package demo` on line 1, so the `if (checked > 0)` statement is on line 6. That line is executed when the test calls `route(4)`, making its instruction count nonzero. The new assertion incorrectly requires it to be zero and causes the test to fail.
generated-coordinate-no-leading-lf-wrong.evidence: `write_text` writes the string without a leading newline; counting the supplied lines places `if (checked > 0) return 1` on line 6, and the JUnit assertion invokes `route(4)`.
generated-coordinate-no-leading-lf-wrong.suggestion: Assert coverage for the actually unexecuted generated source line, or update the expected count for line 6 to reflect the executed branch.

generated-coordinate-leading-lf-wrong.title: Executed Kotlin line is asserted uncovered
generated-coordinate-leading-lf-wrong.description: The generated Kotlin starts with a newline, so the `if (checked > 0)` statement is on one-based source line 7. The test calls `route(4)`, making that condition execute; its instruction counter should not be zero. This assertion therefore fails against the described real JaCoCo counters.
generated-coordinate-leading-lf-wrong.evidence: `rows[7]` refers to generated Kotlin source line 7, which is `if (checked > 0) return 1`; the immediately preceding JUnit assertion invokes `Route().route(4)`.
generated-coordinate-leading-lf-wrong.suggestion: Assert that the executed line has a positive instruction count, or check the intended uncovered line instead.

generated-source-leading-newline.title: The assertion checks a line executed by the test
generated-source-leading-newline.description: The triple-quoted Kotlin source begins with a newline, so `return 1` is generated source line 8. The supplied JUnit assertion calls `route(4)`, making `checked > 0` true and executing that return. The runner maps covered instructions to one-based source lines, so `rows[8]["ci"]` should be nonzero and this assertion fails.
generated-source-leading-newline.evidence: The generated source has a leading newline; counting its lines places `return 1` at line 8. The JUnit input calls `Route().route(4)`, which takes the positive branch and executes that instruction.
generated-source-leading-newline.suggestion: Assert that line 8 has covered instructions, or check an actually uncovered source line.

generated-source-escaped.title: Asserts that an executed return line is uncovered
generated-source-escaped.description: The generated Kotlin source maps `return 1` to one-based source line 7. The supplied JUnit input calls `route(4)`, so `checked > 0` succeeds and that return instruction is covered. Consequently, `rows[7]["ci"]` should not be asserted as zero.
generated-source-escaped.evidence: Applying the literal `\n` escapes gives `if (checked > 0) return 1` on line 6 and `return 1` on line 7. `route(4)` takes that branch.
generated-source-escaped.suggestion: Assert the expected covered instruction count for line 7, or check an actually uncovered executable line.

generated-source-dedent.title: Assertion expects a covered instruction to have zero coverage
generated-source-dedent.description: Calling `route(4)` makes `checked > 0` true, so the `return 1` instruction on generated source line 7 executes. Its `ci` count is therefore nonzero, and this assertion fails.
generated-source-dedent.evidence: After `textwrap.dedent(...).lstrip("\n")`, generated line 7 is `if (checked > 0) return 1`; the supplied JUnit input calls `route(4)`, which takes that branch.
generated-source-dedent.suggestion: Assert that line 7 has positive instruction coverage, or check an actually uncovered line such as the `return -1` instruction on line 8.

generated-source-wrong-leading-newline.title: Assertion targets the wrong generated source line
generated-source-wrong-leading-newline.description: The triple-quoted Kotlin string begins with a newline, so the first source line is blank: the `if (checked > 0)` statement is on one-based line 8, while line 7 contains `val checked = value`. The assertion therefore checks coverage of the assignment rather than the conditional instruction and can pass without proving the intended branch is uncovered.
generated-source-wrong-leading-newline.evidence: The leading newline in `kotlin = """\n package demo...` is preserved by `write_bytes`; the runner maps covered instructions to one-based source lines, making the `if` line 8. The changed assertion reads `rows[7]`.
generated-source-wrong-leading-newline.suggestion: Assert against the one-based source line containing the conditional, or derive the line number from the generated source.
